exact_statement: Over Q(q), with q_i=q^(d_i) generic, suppose chosen type-one Cartan/E/F operators satisfy all toral and mixed [E_i,F_j] relations, with each single-color action integrable. Then BOTH quantum Serre sums of order n=1−a_ij hold, including cubic affine e2. This theorem uses no already-imposed Serre relation.
exact_strategy: Use the fixed rank-one Hopf action on Hom(W,W-prime). For a finite U_i-submodule W and F_j(W), let W-prime be its finite U_i-envelope; it is finite by the rank-one commutator alone: reorder any word on a homogeneous vector into F_i^a E_i^b K_i^c; E_i^b vanishes for large b, each of the finitely many E_i^b vectors has a finite F_i nilpotence bound, and K is scalar on each weight. Thus finitely many F_i^a E_i^b span its envelope, before any multi-color Serre relation is used. Apply the finite generic rank-one string decomposition to this envelope. The restricted operator F_j has adjoint K weightm=−a_ij and is killed by adjoint E_i: adE(T)=(E_iT−TE_i)K_i, so the mixed commutator gives0. Thus it is a highest vector in the finite integrable Hom module, and adF^(m+1) F_j=0 there by the finite rank-one string theorem. Since W contains any chosen vector, this is an operator identity on the whole module. In our coproduct adF(T)=F_i T−K_i T K_i^-1 F_i. Induction with the Gaussian Pascal formula gives adF^n F_j=Σ_r(−1)^r q_i^(r(m−n+1))[n choose r]_i F_i^(n−r)F_jF_i^r. The induction coefficients are q_i^r[n r]+q_i^(r−n−1)[n,r−1]=[n+1,r]. At n=m+1 the exponent is0, exactly the negative Serre sum. Apply the unsigned Chevalley interchange E↔F,K↔K^-1 to get the positive sum. This is the complete KMPY AppendixB finite-Hom proof transported to our coproduct, not its omitted locally-finite lemma as an assumption.
